title: Tesla's Missing Autopilot Data Showed It Detected A Hazard Before Fatal Crash, Despite Claims It Was Missing

reading.body:
A Tesla vehicle operating under Autopilot control was involved in a fatal crash. Tesla told the family of the deceased that crash data from the vehicle was not available. A hacker later demonstrated that the data had been retained in the vehicle's systems, contradicting Tesla's claim to the family.

The failure is a form of data suppression in a deployed autonomous driving system. Tesla had access to information relevant to understanding why the collision occurred but did not make it available during the immediate aftermath, when it would have been most useful for investigation and for the family's understanding of the incident. Catching this would have required either a transparent data retention protocol or an independent technical audit of what information the vehicle actually stored.

It is not established what Tesla's intentions were in representing the data as unavailable, or under what circumstances the data was later recovered and reviewed.
